developments: Zcash fell about 12% on Tuesday and briefly traded below $1,000 for the first time since early September, as Grayscale trust redemptions added selling.
Bitcoin's low on Tuesday was deeper than first reported, about $72,640 on Coinbase, but it closed the day near $73,800, above the $73,000 line analysts were watching.
The US 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.00% after the hot inflation report, and the Nasdaq fell 0.7% with Nvidia down 5.5%.
briefing.changed: Last night's question was whether bitcoin's daily close would hold $73,000. It did, so the line held for now. The new damage is in Zcash, which lost more than bitcoin on the same macro shock.
briefing.question: Is Zcash's fall mostly forced selling from Grayscale trust redemptions and leverage, or a broader turn in demand after the NU7 upgrade rally?
briefing.watch: US PPI on Friday 13 November at 13:30 UK. The next big event is the Fed decision on Wednesday 9 December at 19:00 UK.

lead.headline: Zcash briefly breaks below $1,000 as bitcoin clings to $73,000
lead.standfirst: Zcash fell about 12% in a day, its sharpest drop in weeks, while bitcoin dipped to a near three-month low before closing just above a level traders had marked as critical.
body: Zcash fell as low as $999.57 on Tuesday, its weakest level since early September, Seeking Alpha and Bitcoin.com News reported. The token was down about 12% over 24 hours and roughly 41% below its 2026 high of $1,695, reached on 26 September.

Seeking Alpha linked the fall to leveraged long positions being forced shut and to continuing redemptions from the Grayscale Zcash Trust, which require the trust to sell or withdraw the coins it holds. The same day, Grayscale launched a $1 million Zcash ecosystem programme, with $400,000 in first grants.

Bitcoin also hit its lowest level since late August. Coinbase data showed a low of $72,643 at 16:38 UTC on Tuesday, Forbes reported, after October's US inflation figures came in hotter than forecast. It recovered to about $73,800 by midnight UTC, according to KuCoin market data.

The pressure came from bond markets as well. The US 10-year Treasury yield rose about 14 basis points to 5.00%, TheStreet reported, and the Nasdaq fell 0.74%. Fed Vice Chair Michelle Bowman said in a speech that inflation progress had stalled and that policy was "not on a preset course".
Selling by large holders added to the mood. Bitcoin miner MARA said it had sold 13,597 bitcoin, about $1.1 billion, since 30 September and planned to sell more, CoinDesk reported.
Traders now look to US producer prices on Friday and the Fed's decision on 9 December.

headline: Zcash fell about 12% and briefly broke $1,000, while bitcoin dipped to about $72,640 before closing near $73,800. US 10-year yields hit 5% and the miner MARA said it has sold $1.1 billion of bitcoin since September.
spoken: Good morning. The mood is risk off. Zcash fell about twelve per cent on Tuesday and briefly dropped below one thousand dollars, its lowest since early September, with Grayscale trust redemptions and forced selling blamed. Bitcoin touched about seventy two thousand six hundred dollars, its lowest since August, but closed the day near seventy three thousand eight hundred. US ten year bond yields reached five per cent after the hot inflation report. The miner MARA said it has sold about one point one billion dollars of bitcoin since the end of September. Next to watch is US producer prices on Friday at half past one UK time. Information only, not advice.

stories.title: Zcash falls about 12% and briefly trades below $1,000
stories.why: ZEC hit $999.57, its lowest since early September and about 41% below its 26 September high of $1,695. On Monday it was near $1,165, so the fall has sped up. Seeking Alpha cites forced selling of leveraged longs and Grayscale Zcash Trust redemptions, which add spot selling.
stories.caveat: Liquidation figures for ZEC differ: Seeking Alpha gives about $16.5m across crypto in its window, while Analytics Insight puts ZEC liquidations at about $33m.

note.read: ZEC fell more than twice as far as bitcoin on the same macro shock, so this looks like crowded positioning unwinding after the NU7 rally rather than Zcash-specific bad news.
note.alt: Holders may be taking profits after the upgrade they were waiting for, a 'sell the news' pattern that can last longer than a leverage flush.
note.change: Redemptions from the Grayscale trust stopping, or ZEC holding $1,000 on a further bitcoin dip, would point to forced selling being done.

stories.title: Bitcoin's low was about $72,640, but the daily close held above $73,000
stories.why: Coinbase showed a low of $72,643 at 16:38 UTC on Tuesday, the weakest since about 21 August. Bitcoin then closed the UTC day near $73,800, so the $73,000 close analysts flagged held. They name $70,000 as the next level below and $74,500 to $75,000 as the zone to reclaim.

note.read: Buyers defended $73,000 on a closing basis, but with ETF and miner selling still running, that defence rests on thin demand.
note.alt: The intraday break below $73,000 may already have cleared the stops below it, which sometimes marks a short-term low.
note.change: A daily close below $72,600 would undo the hold; a close back above $75,000 would ease the pressure.

stories.title: US 10-year yield closes at 5.00%; Nasdaq falls 0.7% as Nvidia drops 5.5%
stories.why: The 10-year yield rose about 14 basis points on the inflation report and the 2-year about 18 basis points to 4.73%. The S&P 500 fell 0.38% and the Nasdaq 0.74%. A 5% risk-free yield makes non-yielding assets like bitcoin less attractive to hold. US bond markets are closed today for Veterans Day.

note.read: Bitcoin's moves have been following rates more than stocks this week, so yields are the gauge to watch.
note.alt: Part of the Nasdaq fall was Nvidia-specific (an internal investigation into its chief executive), not rates.
note.change: A soft PPI print on Friday pulling the 10-year back below 4.9% would ease pressure on crypto.

stories.title: Miner MARA has sold 13,597 bitcoin since September and plans to sell more
stories.why: MARA said with its third-quarter results that it sold about $1.1 billion of bitcoin after 30 September, repaid $750m of bitcoin-backed loans, and will keep selling to fund AI infrastructure, debt and possible buybacks. It held 34,012 BTC at 30 September. Steady selling from a large holder adds supply while ETF demand is weak.

stories.title: ETF outflows slow to about $95m on Tuesday; IBIT redemptions continue
stories.why: Early figures show a net outflow of about $95m, with IBIT down $78m, Fidelity's FBTC down $37m and Morgan Stanley's MSBT up $20m. That is smaller than Monday's $201m, but it would be IBIT's eighth straight day of redemptions. Outflows since 2 November are about $1.5bn.
stories.caveat: Tuesday's figures come from a single tracker reported by TechFlow and are not yet confirmed by Farside or SoSoValue.

stories.title: Fed's Bowman: inflation progress has stalled, policy 'not on a preset course'
stories.why: Vice Chair Bowman said core PCE inflation likely rose to 3.3% in October and there is "still work to do", but stopped short of backing a hike and said tightening must be weighed against costs such as housing. She is often among the more dovish officials, so a hawkish tone from her narrows the case for a pause.

stories.title: Zcash NU8 proposal: 8MB blocks, Tachyon shielded pool, quantum-resistant options
stories.why: Developer ValarDragon proposed NU8 for a late January 2027 window, including a Tachyon pool designed against future quantum decryption and a fourfold block size rise. It is still in technical review, core engineer str4d has raised objections, and it would need a community vote.

explained.title: Why trust redemptions can push a coin's price down
body: A trust like Grayscale's Zcash fund holds real coins on behalf of its shareholders. When investors redeem shares, the trust has to sell or hand over coins to pay them, which puts those coins onto the market.
If many holders redeem at once, that selling arrives on top of normal trading, and in a smaller market like Zcash it can move the price more than it would for bitcoin.

investigating: How much ZEC is the Grayscale trust releasing? Evidence: the trust's published holdings over the coming days.
Was Tuesday IBIT's eighth straight day of outflows? Evidence: Farside or SoSoValue figures for 10 November.
Is The Wire missing overnight headlines? Its last refresh was 00:53 UTC, so news after that came from web searches.
corrections: Last night's edition (10 Nov, 19:45) said bitcoin's low was near $73,400. Coinbase data reported by Forbes shows a deeper low of $72,643 at 16:38 UTC.
